facility._amendments_summary: Three executed amendments have progressively TIGHTENED the Maximum Net Leverage Ratio covenant while leaving rate, amortization (0.60%/month, unchanged throughout) and maturity untouched: First Amendment (exec. 2025-08-01, eff. 2025-08-05) cut the cap 6.00x -> 5.75x and added an unquantified cloud-migration capex basket. Second Amendment (exec. 2026-01-20, eff. 2026-01-31) cut it 5.75x -> 5.25x, added an unquantified customer-data-license investment basket, and required enhanced AR-aging reporting. Third Amendment (exec. 2026-04-20, eff. 2026-04-30) cut it 5.25x -> 5.00x and preserved the undrawn revolver commitment from clawback in exchange for undefined 'revised-reporting controls'. All three are pure covenant-reset amendments with a small bundled accommodation each and explicit no-waiver-or-novation language — none is a waiver, cure, or forbearance (no waiver document exists anywhere in this deal). A fourth, UNSIGNED draft Third Amendment (dated 2026-04-01) had proposed a materially tighter 4.75x cap with several terms left open; the version actually executed 19 days later settled at a looser 5.00x — the borrower negotiated MORE headroom than the lender's own opening draft, which is the reverse of the usual pre-signing tightening pattern and worth independent follow-up (documents alone don't explain why).
facility._note: Three executed amendments in this deal (vs. zero for Talvorn and one-plus-an-expired-waiver for Selvara) is the most extensive amendment chain in this batch — see our_view for what the resulting covenant trend actually shows.

our_view.thesis_status: Compliant every quarter since close (6 of 6 quarterly tests passed), but covenant HEADROOM has compressed sharply — from ~13% at close (Q1'25: 0.7709x cushion vs a 6.00x max) to ~2% by Q2'26 (0.1038x cushion vs a 5.00x max) — because three amendments (Aug'25, Jan'26, Apr'26) have ratcheted the covenant ceiling down faster than actual leverage has improved (Net Leverage: 5.23x -> 5.21x -> 5.28x -> 5.31x -> 5.13x [as-filed, pre-restatement] -> 4.90x). TTM Covenant EBITDA itself dipped through 2025 (from $33.3M at Q1'25 to $30.9M at Q4'25) before recovering to $32.2M by Q2'26 — so the underlying operating trend is closer to stable-to-improving than the covenant math alone suggests, but the covenant ratchet has been the dominant force, not EBITDA growth. A March 2026 restatement (an omitted $492K revenue / $39K EBITDA milestone) and a Q1 2026 compliance certificate that was never formally re-issued after that correction is the underwriting's 'reporting discipline' pillar's first real test, and it did not go cleanly — this, combined with three renegotiations in 15 months, is a materially different risk profile from a clean, unamended credit.
our_view.what_would_change_our_mind: A fourth consecutive quarter of TTM Covenant EBITDA decline; any quarterly Net Leverage print within 0.05x of the then-current maximum; a second reporting/restatement event or a documentation gap on a re-certification; or loss/non-renewal of a top-10 customer given how thin the remaining covenant cushion now is.
